title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary

This document consolidates the product overview, PRD, design specifications, roadmap & themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the "Unified Inference" initiative. Unified Inference is Redwood Inference's cross-environment runtime and control plane that provides a consistent developer API, predictable SLOs, and cost-aware routing across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals

- Provide a single product surface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with uniform semantics across deployment modes.
- Deliver predictable latency and throughput SLOs for customers via routing, dedicated capacity, and autoscaling.
- Reduce unit cost for customers through batching, caching, and model/quantization recommendations.
- Enable enterprise requirements (VPC, KMS, audit logs, compliance evidence) for Private deployments.

Success metrics (12 months)

1. Increase platform adoption: convert 30% of self-serve accounts with moderate usage to Dedicated trials.
2. Latency: 95th percentile token latency <= 120ms for standard generation workloads on Hosted for small-to-medium models.
3. Cost efficiency: 20% reduction in per-token cost for recommended workloads using Optimize suggestions.
4. Reliability: Achieve 99.95% uptime for Dedicated customers (SLA).
5. Enterprise readiness: complete compliance evidence bundle for SOC2 and ISO by end of Q3.

Target Personas

- ML Engineers: model serving, quality monitoring, evals, and model rollout.
- Software Engineers: integrate SDKs, low-latency endpoints, and streaming.
- Platform/Infrastructure Engineers: capacity planning, autoscaling, and routing policies for cost and redundancy.

Product Requirements (PRD) - Must have

1. API parity: REST/SDK endpoints for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with streaming support and function/tool calling.
2. Model catalog: curated list of verified open models plus Redwood-recommended variants (quantized, fp16). Each model entry includes memory footprint, latency profile, token cost estimate, and fallbacks.
3. Routing policies: configurable by customer (latency-first, cost-first, region, custom tags) with automated fallback to compatible variants.
4. Dedicated pools: reserved GPU capacity with autoscaling, burst policies, and SLA definitions.
5. Private deployment: control plane options for VPC, on-prem package with KMS/HSM integration, and audit logging.
6. Observability: per-route token/cost breakdown, trace hooks, and quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
7. Optimize integrations: batching/caching suggestions, quantization recommendations, and workload analysis UI.
8. Security: RBAC, SSO (SAML/OIDC), encryption at rest, and key rotation guidance.

Design Specifications (high level)

- API & Schema
  - Maintain compatibility with existing Redwood API shapes. New fields must be additive.
  - Streaming: server-sent events (SSE) for text streams; chunked transfer for SDK fallbacks.
  - Function calling: structured JSON schema enforcement with best-effort validation in the control plane.

- Runtime Behavior
  - Model selection: control plane selects a serving variant based on routing policy, sequence length hint, and capacity.
  - Batching: continuous batching window configurable per-customer; default 10ms with adaptive extension under high QPS.
  - Cache: prefix/KV caching with TTL controls; cacheable response types documented in API guide.

- Observability
  - Per-token metrics: emit tokens_generated, tokens_cached_hit, tokens_batched_count, and cost_estimate as tags.
  - Instrumentation: trace spans for request routing, model load, kernel execution, and postprocessing.

- Configuration and Defaults
  - Default routing: latency-first across hosted regions, fall back to cost-first during peak overload.
  - Autoscaling policy: min=1, target_util=70%, cooldown=2m, max_burst=2x for Dedicated pools.

Non-functional Requirements

- Scalability: handle 10x current peak QPS within 9 months by incremental autoscaling and additional Dedicated regions.
- Security & Compliance: endpoints and control plane must meet SOC2-required controls for change management and access logging.
- Backwards compatibility: any breaking changes require a 90-day deprecation notice and migration guide.

Roadmap & Themes (quarterly view)

Q2 2027 - Foundation and Pilot
- Complete model catalog and perf profiles for top 12 models.
- Launch Dedicated reserved pools beta with 3 enterprise customers.
- Basic Optimize suggestions (batch size and cache recommendations).

Q3 2027 - Enterprise & Private
- Private deployment: VPC control plane beta and KMS integration.
- SLA definitions and billing pipeline for Dedicated customers.
- Release improved routing policies and canary rollouts.

Q4 2027 - Optimize & Observability
- Launch Redwood Optimize v2: automated quantization suggestions and workload classifier.
- Per-route quality regression alerts and prompt-set driven evals.
- Fine-grained cost allocation in Console.

Q1 2028 - Scale & Global Regions
- Expand Dedicated regions in APAC and EU zones.
- Autoscaling improvements and enhanced burst handling.
- Private on-prem packaging improvements for air-gapped installs.

Pricing & Packaging Notes

Pricing principles:
- Transparent per-unit pricing for Hosted (tokens and embeddings) with predictable bucketed discounts for committed Dedicated capacity.
- Dedicated pricing composed of: reserved GPU capacity fee + per-token execution fee for overages.
- Private deployments are licensed (platform fee + support tier) with optional managed services.

Suggested pricing tiers (examples for sales guidance):

- Hosted (self-serve)
  - Pay-as-you-go: $0.0006 per token generated (baseline model), $0.003 per 1k embedding units.
  - Developer: volume discounts at 20k+ monthly token units.

- Dedicated (example commit structure)
  - Small pool (4 GPUs reserved): $7,500/month + $0.00045 per token overage.
  - Medium pool (16 GPUs): $26,000/month + $0.0004 per token overage.
  - Negotiated enterprise pricing for >64 GPU commitments with custom SLAs.

- Private
  - Platform license: annual fee based on seats and supported nodes.
  - Support tiers: Standard (business hours), Premium (24/7) with response SLAs.

Discounting and packaging guidance for sales:
- Encourage 12-month reserved commitments with a 10-18% discount vs month-to-month.
- Offer a 3-month migration pilot discounted with refundable credits applied to first-year committed purchase.

Release Notes - 2028-02-20 (v2.1)

Highlights:
- General availability of Unified Inference v2.1 with:
  - Improved routing engine with region-aware cost heuristics.
  - Dedicated autoscaling improvements (faster scaling under burst).
  - Optimize v2 launch: automated quantization suggestions and interactive workload analyzer.
  - Private control plane release: VPC-first configuration and KMS support for on-prem preview customers.

Migration notes and breaking changes:
1. API: New optional parameter "sequence_hint" added to generation endpoints. No breaking changes; clients can ignore the field.
2. Billing: Dedicated overage meter now reports pre-quantization token counts by default; there is a transitional 30-day window for customers to opt-in to post-quantization metering.
3. Rollouts: Canary routing default window shortened from 10 minutes to 5 minutes; teams using custom canary settings may need to revalidate their policies.

Rollout plan:
- Day 0: Gradual rollout to 10% of Hosted traffic for latency-first routing tests. Monitor key metrics (95p latency, error rate, token cost).
- Day 3: Increase to 50% pending health signals.
- Day 7: Full rollout for Hosted.
- Dedicated: staged enablement per customer with migration assistance.
- Private: GA for VPC control plane; on-prem customers scheduled via account teams.

Operational runbook highlights:
- Monitoring: dashboard "Unified Inference / Production Overview" includes 95p latency, tokens/sec, cache-hit-rate, queue-length, and per-model failure rates.
- Alert thresholds: 95p latency > 200ms sustained for 5m (severity P2), cache-hit-rate < 20% (P3), model load failures > 1% (P1).
- Escalation: follow eng-sre incident playbook; contact owners: eng-serving-runtime (primary), eng-sre (secondary).

Open risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Model performance variability across hardware variants. Mitigation: maintain per-variant perf profiles and automated fallback to stable variants.
- Risk: Billing complexity with quantized models. Mitigation: provide visibility in Console and 30-day opt-in transition period.
- Risk: Private deployment compatibility across customer environments. Mitigation: expanded reference architectures, onprem packaging improvements, and dedicated solutions engineering time per customer.

Ownership & Next Steps

- Product owner: Ava Chen.
- Engineering leads: Miguel Alvarez (serving runtime), Priya Rao (platform & routing), Ethan Brooks (Optimize).

  2. Enable billing transition opt-in flows in Console and notify impacted customers. (Owner: finance-and-legal + product)
  3. Start Closed Beta for Private on-prem improvements with 2 pilot customers. (Owner: eng-private-deployments)
